title: Ops Resilience Handshake Toolkit
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, pragmatic project plan and toolkit to operationalize SLO-driven releases across platform, serving-runtime, product, and SRE. Goal is to create repeatable ‘handshakes’ (pre-release checks, canary gating, and post-release validation) so feature teams can ship without surprise reliability regressions.

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: model-serving routes (text-generation API + embeddings) + control-plane deploys that affect routing/rollouts.
- Out of scope: bulk infrastructure purchases, non-API customer billing systems.
- Constraint: non-root access in private clusters; experiments should be safe with traffic shaping only.

What success looks like (12-week outcomes):
- 80% of new feature rollouts use the handshake checklist & resilience runners pipeline.
- Detect and automatically rollback 90% of SLO regressions in canary stage without human intervention.
- Reduce production P95 latency regressions attributed to new code by 60% vs baseline.

Core concepts / new terms used here:
- Handshake: a documented set of checks (SLO smoke, chaos-lite probe, dependency health) completed before wide rollout.
- Resilience runner: a small synthetic runbook that executes pre-configured synthetic traffic + assertions against SLO signals. Runs in CI and during canary.
- Gamma cohort: ~5% of real traffic routed to canary to validate signals before 25% staging ramp.
- Traffic-shaper: platform component to route and throttle traffic to canaries and cohorts.

High-level flow (simple):
1) Feature author creates a resilience runner and links to PR.
2) CI runs runner against test environment (synthetic + golden prompt set).
3) If CI passes, feature moves to canary with Gamma cohort (5%).
4) Handshake checks run: synthetic runner, SLO smoke (latency/availability/error rate), dependency health.
5) Automated gating: pass -> ramp to 25% -> monitor 24h -> full release; fail -> automatic rollback and incident stub creation.

Minimal SLO set for handshake (examples teams must implement for each relevant route):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% successful responses (2xx/stream-api-ok) over 7d window with a 1h burn rate compute for canary windows.
- Latency SLO: P95 < 320ms for short-text model routes, P95 < 700ms for long-context flows (1000-token).
- Error budget guardrail: during canary, allow at most 25% of daily error budget burn; trigger rollback if exceeded for two consecutive 30m windows.
- Model-quality guardrail: embedding cosine drop of >0.06 on golden set or generation perplexity/stability delta >15% triggers review.

Stakeholders and responsibilities (handshake roles):
- Feature owner (FE/ML engineer): author resilience runner, define golden prompt set, provide expected perf targets.
- Platform-engineering (owner: Asha Patel): provide traffic-shaper, canary orchestration, and reviewer for runner infra.
- Serving-runtime team (Rina Chen): guarantee runtime telemetry hooks (kv cache hit, concurrency, batching stats).
- SRE (Diego Morales): own alert thresholds, rollback automation, incident stub templates.
- Product/Design (Owen Gallagher): sign-off for user-facing quality guardrails.

Deliverables by week (8-week pilot then iteration):
- Week 0–1: Kickoff, identify 3 pilot features (text generation route, embeddings route, routing-control API).
- Week 2: Resilience runner template published (YAML + runner script + example golden set).
- Week 3: Traffic-shaper alpha deployed to staging; basic Gamma cohort traffic routing enabled.
- Week 4: CI integration: runners run automatically for PRs targeting pilot features.
- Week 5: Canary automation: single-click canary start/stop + rollback hook implemented.
- Week 6: Observability dashboard: per-canary SLO dashboard and burn-rate widget.
- Week 7: Run 3 pilot canaries; refine thresholds and rollback rules.
- Week 8: Retrospective + rollout plan to additional teams + docs.

Checklist: (minimum for a successful handshake)
- [ ] Resilience runner present in PR with golden prompt set.
- [ ] CI-run passes for synthetic and k6-style load (script attached).
- [ ] Serving-runtime telemetry linked (latency histograms, error counters, kv-hit rate).
- [ ] Canary started to Gamma cohort and handshake checks completed.
- [ ] No SLO guardrail tripped during 2h observation OR automated rollback performed and incident stub created.
- [ ] Post-canary notes added to Confluence page.

Automation & tooling tasks (short list):
- Integrate runner execution into GitHub Actions and expose results as check runs.
- Implement a small lambda that consumes SLO burn-rate and posts pass/fail to canary orchestrator.
- Add a canary toggle to Console with Gamma/25/100% presets and an override for emergency rollback.
- Publish runner templates + sample golden sets in mono-repo under /platform/resilience-runners.

Experiments and validation plan (what to measure):
- Canary sensitivity: how many true regressions are detected in Gamma cohort vs missed until 25%?
- False positive rate: how often does automated rollback fire unnecessarily?
- Mean time to rollback (MTTRollback): target < 6 minutes for automated cases.
- SLO delta uplift: measure P95 across baseline vs post-handshake rollouts.

Risk matrix and mitigations:
- Risk: false rollbacks during expected traffic spikes. Mitigation: additive traffic smoothing + sample-aware thresholds and short grace windows.
- Risk: teams skip creating golden sets. Mitigation: require a minimal default golden set auto-generated from prior production samples when missing.
- Risk: rollout automation bugs cause stale toggles. Mitigation: safety checks and manual override in Console.

Runbook sketch for handshake failure (short):
1) Canary alarm -> runbook stub auto-populates incident with logs and run metadata.
2) SRE triage: validate signals (is this an infra blip?).
3) If burn rate verified -> trigger automated rollback, page oncall, notify feature owner and platform lead.
4) Postmortem owner assigned automatically to feature owner + SRE.

Communications and meeting cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync during pilot (Feature owners + Platform + SRE).
- Post-canary report in #ops-resilience with structured template (what ran, pass/fail, metrics snapshot).
- Monthly reliability review: aggregated SLO regressions, root causes, and action items.

Nitty-gritty notes / implementation details (practical tips):
- Use short golden sets (10–25 prompts) for quick smoke; keep an extended set for nightly regression runs.
- Prefer deterministic seeds for generation checks to make diffs meaningful.
- Tag telemetry with canary_id + commit_sha for rapid correlation.
- If a canary fails within first 10 minutes, consider immediate rollback without waiting full window.

Next actions (for the first working session):
- Platform to create traffic-shaper sandbox and open GH PR for runner template (Asha).
- SRE to author CI check run schema and provide alert thresholds (Diego).
- Serving-runtime to add canary tags to telemetry (Rina).
- Pick pilot features and schedule first canary for Week 3.

Open questions (to decide in kickoff):
- Burn-rate algorithm specifics for short windows (simple vs Bayesian smoothing).
- Standardized minimal golden set format (JSONL vs YAML).
- How to handle model-version compatibility between canary and fallback variant.

Appendix: useful references and example snippets
- Example runner invocation: runner.sh --env=staging --golden=golden.jsonl --assert=latency,p95:320
- Example canary policy comment for PR: /canary gamma=5% watch=2h auto-rollback=true

Notes to self: keep this doc short and focused — teams hate long 'playbooks' they don't use. Aim to ship a thin first iteration that runs and collects data.
